quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2026 segments outside Intelligent Infrastructure (CFO Greg Hebard): Regulated Industries revenue $3.2B, up 4% YoY and above outlook, with the upside primarily from Automotive & Transportation where demand was stronger than expected; core operating margin 5.6% (+10 bps). Connected Living and Digital Commerce revenue $1.4B, up 5% YoY and above outlook, largely from Connected Living where consumer-related demand beat the cautious assumptions in the guide; core operating margin 4.9%. Company GAAP operating income $445M (5.1% of revenue); core operating income $504M.
quarterly_data.figure: Regulated Industries $3.2B (+4%), margin 5.6%; CLDC $1.4B (+5%), margin 4.9%; core op income $504M

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 and FY2026 end-market outlook: CFO: Q4 Regulated Industries revenue approximately $3.3B, up 6% YoY (Healthcare & Packaging stable, Renewables improving, Automotive & Transportation better than expected earlier in the year); Q4 Connected Living and Digital Commerce approximately $1.4B, roughly flat YoY; core tax rate approximately 21%. CEO: FY2026 revenue now approximately $35B, up from the March outlook of $34B, roughly 17% growth; FY2026 Auto revenue approximately $4.4B (March outlook $4.2B); Connected Living approximately $2.7B (up $300M from the March outlook); Digital Commerce approximately $2.7B (up $100M), 'one of our higher margin end markets'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 Regulated ~$3.3B (+6%), CLDC ~$1.4B; FY26 ~$35B (vs $34B March, ~17%); Auto ~$4.4B; Connected Living ~$2.7B; Digital Commerce ~$2.7B

quarterly_data.signal: Regulated Industries views (CEO Mike Dastoor): Auto beat its outlook on 'stronger export demand from China, industry consolidation, and growth in powertrain-agnostic platforms', but 'we remain cautious on the Automotive market given continued demand volatility'. Renewables improving on 'safe harbor projects, demand for power tied to AI and data center infrastructure, and a shift from residential towards commercial projects'. Healthcare: the FY2026 outlook was taken down by $100M ('I wouldn't put too much into that'; daily shipments add up to $125M-$130M); long-term view unchanged (GLP-1s, drug delivery, continuous glucose monitors, med devices); 'FY 2027 should show some level of growth'; the Croatia site comes online right at the end of FY2027, so it will be an FY2028 event; capability-driven M&A and more vertical integration continue.

FY2027 total-company framing: CEO: full-year FY2027 guidance comes in September; the AI comment 'was more to give the street a little bit of idea of what's going on in our AI piece. There's puts and takes on the other side of the business' — 'I wouldn't start expanding revenue on an incremental basis to what I've already said on the AI revenue' and 'I want to make sure that we don't get carried away with the numbers'. Component availability, mix, prioritizing margins, customer ramp timing, free cash flow and returns will shape the full year. CFO: 'Typically, Q4 is our highest margin quarter'; Jabil expects to keep improving gross margins and getting SG&A leverage to reach 6%+ 'and higher from there'.

North Carolina capacity (CEO): 'We booked one customer. We're talking to others'; more guidance on North Carolina in September. On the additional land next door, Jabil is 'looking at facilities which are easier to get to, as in readily available' — capacity that is already built out rather than 'another 12, 18 months of build-out'. CFO: 'we're real confident we could have that revenue in place from a footprint perspective' for the FY2027 AI growth.
